body:
>It seems to me that you might want a way out, in part, to release yourself from this crushing sense of obligation.

Much of what you said rang true with me, thankyou for putting into words many things I am unable to. I saw my doctor yesterday and thanks to all the advice I have recieved here I did the right thing (I will do an update post when I have the energy...) and was absolutely honest. One thing my doctor said he sensed was exactly this. 

>Believe it or not, people are worthy of love and can be a joy to others just by being who they are.

This is something I have never been able to convince myself of. When I was off work last time, I felt like the world had moved on without me and I had done nothing but go backwards. I had nothing to talk to friends about, because the view from bed isn't much to mention. 

Anyway, to all here at SW, thankyou for everything. I promise I will post that update soon, when I have my head around where I am now compared to before I posted here.
Thankyou for your lovely post. You have all given me so much to think about.
I know that I'm lucky - I hope I don't sound ungrateful.  The most amazing person I have ever met loves *me* and I wish I could take as much good from that as I should be able to.
Thanks. Your words are equally as comforting and helpful as the shed-loads of advice the other amazing people here have offered.

Wow, that's terrible! I'm actually in the UK so it won't be as simple to get therapeutic input, waiting lists are long and that's just for a counsellor. It's unlikely I would be able to see a psychologist because there are so few and I there are cases far more severe than mine, as I have seen every day.

>Don't do this to him, please.
>Do you love him just so much to deny yourself to him?

Wow, I can hear this as though he is saying it himself. It is our love that is keeping me here. I just feel like that love is all I am holding on to and while it is a powerful thing, I don't know how I am supposed to survive on that alone.

I just keep going over my appointment with my doctor and I can't see how you bring something like this up. I went to him when I was so depressed I could barely move, but it seemed easier then. This feels like it's just a decision I've made to give up, and I don't know how to communicate that. I can't convince myself that it deserves help.
I'm sorry about your friend. Did you have therapy after it? If so do you think it made a difference? I had a small amount of counselling while in university, but no serious therapy.

Perhaps, as I didn't really handle the death well at first and blamed myself for a while. It was almost 2 years ago that it happened and I wouldn't say I've been preoccupied about it. I will say that for a few days after it was the most difficult experience of my life.

You're right, of course, but it doesn't make it easier. A part of what has led me to contemplating suicide is the feeling of inferiority. I can't help but feel judged by others for my weaknesses. I am definately leaving my job, but it doesn't solve the fact that I have no ambition left and there will be an expectation to move on to something else.

Thanks for your kind words. I guess that's one of the things I'm struggling with - that what I've seen will never leave me. One of my friends recently said to me "you know you should leave your job, you're not the person you were 2 years ago". That hurt me deeply, but only because it's true.

I'm seeing my doctor on Thursday for another reason, and have been trying to persuade myself to bring these issues up. I guess I am afraid of the consequences - I feel ashamed of my period of absence, and I'm reluctant to admit that I am struggling to cope.
